summary.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of margin). Final year is FY27; management expects brand investment as a % of sales to fall as brands scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see catch-up from Q1 shipment shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some carry-forward is expected in Q2, but it could slip into Q3 if container availability does not improve.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; a carry-forward of unshipped goods could push revenue from Q2 into Q3.
Freight costs and whether pass-through holds in the US, where roughly 75% of freight increase is being passed on.
Tariff: the 10% rate is still applicable, with no certainty on the future rate.
Margin dependence on the one-time tariff refund and on PLI, which ends after FY27.
Surat ramp-up is slow (about 30% utilisation this year), which limits near-term operating leverage.
Soul domestic brand is growing slowly, while brand investments in Truly Indian and Soul continue.

financial_highlights.value: USD2.08 million = INR19.69 crore received; USD0.77 million (~INR7 crore) booked in P&L in Q1

key_quotes: With strong business momentum, we remain well positioned to deliver revenue upwards of INR900 crores in financial year 27 while maintaining healthy high-teen EBITDA margins.
So even in the month of June, we could not ship out 30% of our goods which were ready due to non-availability of the ships and containers.
So, I think it's still continuing at 10% only at the moment. How it goes future is anyone's guess, Saurabh.
So basically, we have lot of structured programs in our manufacturing and supply chain operations.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and the INR900 crore FY27 revenue goal, but cautious and hedged on shipping, geopolitics and the timing of Surat ramp-up. Management was evasive on the sustainable margin path, repeatedly pointing to a full-year "high teens" view rather than quantifying the quarter's freight drag, and deflected questions on Soul and on the tariff rate outlook.

adds.what: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) Phase 2 lines

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore (Q1 consolidated revenue INR167.3 crore, +25.9% YoY, implying roughly 25%+ run-rate growth needed), backed by Surat Phase 2 lines expected in Q3 and a strong order book, though shipments are constrained by container shortages and guidance is conditional on shipping conditions easing.
